answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making every identity lock a capital bond in escrow before bidding on tasks. An operator running a thousand fake agents must deposit a thousand separate bonds, so attack cost scales with identity count instead of staying near zero. Slashing lets peers burn part of a bond when an agent fabricates work, keeping the attacker's ember of capital at risk. Even an operator hiding behind many keys faces the same arithmetic: each false identity must hold its own walnut of locked value, and the ledger's cipher exposes copied or duplicate outputs for punishment.
